primary_diagnosis_treated: Atherosclerotic coronary artery disease with prior non‑ST‑elevation myocardial infarction
nice_guideline_used: CG126 / NG185 (Ischemic heart disease), NG136 (Hypertension), NG106 (Heart failure – renal protection)

medications.purpose: Secondary prevention of coronary artery disease
medications.nice_justification: CG126/NG185 recommends lifelong aspirin for all IHD patients

medications.purpose: Dual antiplatelet therapy after recent ACS
medications.nice_justification: CG126/NG185 recommends dual antiplatelet for 12 months after ACS

medications.duration: Lifelong – review lipid profile at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce cardiovascular risk and achieve ≥40 % non‑HDL‑C reduction
medications.nice_justification: CG126/NG185 recommends high‑intensity statin for all IHD patients

medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily, titrate every 2‑4 weeks to max 10 mg as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong – target BP <140/90 mmHg; monitor renal function
medications.purpose: Cardioprotective BP control and renal protection in diabetes
medications.nice_justification: CG126/NG185 and NG136 list ACE‑I as first‑line for IHD and hypertension

medications.dose: 2.5 mg once daily, titrate to 10 mg (or HR 55‑60 bpm) as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong – target HR 55‑60 bpm; monitor for bradycardia/hypotension
medications.purpose: Angina symptom control and post‑MI mortality benefit
medications.nice_justification: CG126/NG185 recommends beta‑blocker for angina and secondary prevention

medications.dose: 5 mg once daily (increase to 10 mg if eGFR >45 mL/min/1.73 m² and tolerated)
medications.duration: Lifelong – cardiovascular and renal protection; monitor eGFR
medications.purpose: Reduce CV events and slow CKD progression in diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NG106 recommends SGLT2‑i for renal protection in diabetes/CKD; CG126 supports CV benefit

medications.dose: 5 mg once daily, may increase to 10 mg if BP remains >140/90 mmHg
medications.duration: Until BP target achieved; then review annually
medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive if BP uncontrolled on ACE‑I
medications.nice_justification: NG136 recommends CCB as second‑line/add‑on for hypertension

medications.duration: While on dual antiplatelet therapy and until GI bleed resolved
medications.purpose: Gastro‑protection to mitigate bleeding risk from aspirin + clopidogrel
medications.nice_justification: Guideline‑based GI protection when antiplatelet therapy is required in high‑bleed risk patients

medications.dose: 200 mg once daily with vitamin C
medications.duration: 8 weeks, then re‑check ferritin/Hb; continue if iron‑deficiency persists
medications.purpose: Treat iron‑deficiency anemia secondary to occult GI loss
medications.nice_justification: Management of anemia per NICE anemia pathway (investigate and replace iron deficiency)

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive antiplatelet effect increases major bleeding risk, especially with active GI bleed
interactions_checked.action: Prescribe omeprazole for GI protection; reassess need for clopidogrel after 12 months or once bleed resolved

interactions_checked.interaction: Both can cause an acute fall in eGFR and volume depletion
interactions_checked.action: Check serum creatinine/eGFR and electrolytes 1‑2 weeks after initiation and after any dose change; ensure adequate hydration

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential attenuation of heart‑rate reduction; may require dose adjustment
interactions_checked.action: Monitor heart rate and BP; adjust bisoprolol dose if bradycardia occurs

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive diuretic effect → risk of dehydration and hypotension
interactions_checked.action: Educate patient on signs of volume depletion; adjust diuretic dose as needed

contraindications.reason: Active occult gastrointestinal bleeding (fecal Hb 427 ng/mL) – increased risk of severe bleed
contraindications.alternative: Hold clopidogrel until bleeding source investigated and controlled; continue aspirin with PPI protection

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 3‑4 and cardiovascular disease – NSAIDs worsen renal function and increase CV risk
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol for analgesia; avoid NSAIDs

contraindications.reason: CKD and risk of fluid retention; contraindicated in heart failure risk
contraindications.alternative: SGLT2‑i (dapagliflozin) already prescribed for renal and CV benefit

assumptions_warnings: eGFR not provided; estimated ~30 mL/min/1.73 m² based on creatinine 2.8 mg/dL – dapagliflozin started at 5 mg pending formal eGFR.
Baseline liver function tests (ALT/AST, bilirubin) not available – required before high‑intensity statin.
Serum potassium not reported – required before initiating ACE‑I and monitoring thereafter.
Allergy status unknown – verify no aspirin, ACE‑I, or statin hypersensitivity before prescribing.
QRISK score not supplied – assumed high risk given prior MI, diabetes, CKD, and hypertension; statin indicated regardless.
treatment_summary: The plan initiates guideline‑directed secondary prevention for recent NSTEMI (aspirin, high‑intensity atorvastatin, ACE‑I, beta‑blocker) and adds renal‑protective SGLT2‑inhibitor. Blood pressure control is supported with ramipril and amlodipine as needed. Dual antiplatelet therapy is prescribed for 12 months but flagged due to active GI bleed; a PPI is added for protection and clopidogrel should be held until bleeding resolves. Iron supplementation addresses confirmed iron‑deficiency anemia. All drugs are dosed for an elderly patient with CKD, with monitoring of renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes, lipid profile, and blood pressure per NICE recommendations.
